title: Terraform Environments and Workspaces
subtitle: Separate dev/test/prod safely with inputs, state boundaries, and promotion discipline

mapResources.label: Open Environments and Workspaces Lab README

nodes.label: Environment
nodes.definition: An environment is a separate deployment context such as dev, test, stage, or production.
nodes.whyItMatters: Different environments need different inputs, safety rules, and state boundaries.
nodes.safeSentence: An environment is a separate place where infrastructure runs, such as dev, test, or production.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not treat dev and prod as just different names if they share risky state or credentials.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Terraform environment strategy is about keeping infrastructure contexts clearly separated so changes do not accidentally affect the wrong place.

note.summary:
Environment means a separate deployment context with separate safety expectations.

Dev: learning/testing
Test/Stage: validation
Prod: real impact

image.caption: Same Terraform pattern can target dev/test/prod safely when inputs and state are separated.

nodes.label: Environment Separation
nodes.definition: Environment separation keeps dev, test, and production from interfering with each other.
nodes.whyItMatters: Separation reduces the chance that a test change damages production.
nodes.safeSentence: Environment separation helps protect production from development or testing changes.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not rely only on memory or naming discipline for production safety.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Teams separate environments using folders, variables, workspaces, backends, permissions, and promotion rules.

note.summary: Use multiple boundaries: folders, tfvars, workspaces, backend paths, accounts, and CI approvals.

nodes.label: Folder Strategy
nodes.definition: Folder strategy means organizing Terraform code into separate folders by environment or component.
nodes.whyItMatters: Folders make environment boundaries visible and reviewable.
nodes.safeSentence: Folder-based environment separation makes the boundaries easy to see and review.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not create confusing folder trees where people cannot tell what environment they are changing.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Some teams use separate folders for dev, test, and prod so each environment has a clear boundary.

nodes.label: Variable Strategy
nodes.definition: Variable strategy controls which values change between environments.
nodes.whyItMatters: The same Terraform pattern may need different sizes, names, tags, or retention settings in each environment.
nodes.safeSentence: Variables let the same Terraform pattern use different values per environment.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not copy entire Terraform projects just to change a few values.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Variables help teams reuse Terraform patterns while changing only the inputs needed for each environment.

note.summary: Typical environment inputs: size, tags, retention, region, thresholds.

nodes.label: tfvars Per Environment
nodes.definition: tfvars files provide environment-specific variable values.
nodes.whyItMatters: They let teams keep reusable Terraform logic separate from environment inputs.
nodes.safeSentence: tfvars files can separate dev, test, and prod values from the reusable configuration.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not commit secrets into tfvars files.
nodes.interviewAnswer: A common pattern is to keep shared Terraform code and pass different tfvars files for dev, test, or production.

nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.definition: A Terraform workspace is a named state instance for the same configuration.
nodes.whyItMatters: Workspaces can separate multiple instances of the same configuration.
nodes.safeSentence: Workspaces can separate state for different instances of the same Terraform configuration.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not assume workspaces are always the best environment strategy.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Workspaces can be useful, but teams need discipline because it must be obvious which workspace is active before planning or applying.

nodes.label: Workspace Caution
nodes.definition: Workspace caution means avoiding accidental changes caused by using the wrong active workspace.
nodes.whyItMatters: A workspace mistake can point Terraform at the wrong state.
nodes.safeSentence: Workspaces are useful, but teams need naming and review discipline.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not run Terraform commands without checking the active workspace in a workspace-based setup.
nodes.interviewAnswer: The main workspace risk is that a user or pipeline plans or applies against the wrong workspace.

note.summary: Safety habits: show active workspace in logs, enforce naming and approvals.

nodes.label: Backend Per Environment
nodes.definition: Backend per environment means each environment stores Terraform state in a separate backend location or state path.
nodes.whyItMatters: Separate state reduces the risk of mixing dev, test, and production changes.
nodes.safeSentence: Separate backends or state paths help reduce the risk of mixing environments.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not let dev and prod accidentally share the same state path.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Teams often separate backend state per environment so production state is not mixed with lower environments.

note.summary: State boundary should match environment boundary (dev path vs prod path).

nodes.label: Promotion
nodes.definition: Promotion means moving a tested Terraform change from lower environments toward production.
nodes.whyItMatters: Promotion lets teams validate changes before production impact.
nodes.safeSentence: A safe Terraform workflow usually tests changes in lower environments before production.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not treat production as the first test environment.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Promotion is the path from dev to test or stage and then to production, usually with review and approval at each step.

note.summary: Typical path: dev plan/test -> stage review -> prod approval/apply.

nodes.label: Wrong Environment Risk
nodes.definition: Wrong environment risk is applying or planning against the wrong environment, workspace, account, or backend.
nodes.whyItMatters: This is one of the most dangerous Terraform mistakes.
nodes.safeSentence: One of the biggest Terraform risks is running a change against the wrong environment or state.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not assume the command line is pointed at the right place.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Before applying Terraform, teams should verify environment, workspace, backend, account, and plan output.

note.summary: Pre-apply checklist: folder, workspace, backend path, account, plan, required approval.

nodes.label: Modules and Reuse
nodes.definition: Open the previous map that explains reusable Terraform modules.
nodes.whyItMatters: Environment strategy often combines modules with different inputs per environment.
nodes.safeSentence: Modules and environment inputs often work together to reuse patterns safely.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not treat this as an environment concept. It is a map doorway.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Modules provide reusable patterns, and environment strategy controls how those patterns are applied safely across dev, test, and production.
